subject.title: [Feature]: Support multi-target cron delivery from configured target sets

question: Should cron fan-out ship as a bounded explicit `delivery.targets` contract first, or should the initial core design also include operator-managed named target sets?
rationale: Both choices introduce public configuration and delivery semantics, but named sets add a distinct persisted control-plane surface beyond the direct dispatch feature.

options.title: Explicit targets first
options.body: Add a backward-compatible target-list form with per-target tracing and session-aware delivery, while leaving named target sets for a separately approved follow-up.

options.title: Include named target sets
options.body: Design an owner-managed target-set configuration and its update, validation, deletion, audit, and upgrade semantics alongside the initial fan-out implementation.

options.title: Keep cron single-target
options.body: Decline core fan-out and require operators to use separate jobs or external orchestration despite duplicated producer execution.

recommendation.title: Explicit targets first
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible target-list form with per-target tracing and session-aware delivery, while leaving named target sets for a separately approved follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged command-cron work is the closest current producer/runtime surface and makes them a strong routing candidate for the contract decision.
